claim_details.claim: Cardiac biomarkers are substances released into the blood when the heart is damaged or stressed they are used to diagnose and monitor heart disease

The most widely used cardiac biomarker is cardiac troponin (troponin T or I), which enters the bloodstream shortly after a heart attack and remains elevated for days, making it the gold standard for detecting myocardial infarction
Other commonly used biomarkers include creatinine kinase (CK), its heart-specific subtype CK-MB myoglobin, although these are less specific and have largely been superseded by troponin measurements

Additional biomarkers used in clinical practice include natriuretic peptides (such as BNP or NT-proBNP), C-reactive protein (CRP) uric acid, each serving different diagnostic and prognostic purposes across various heart conditions
